verdict.rationale: Kommo documents a first-party CRM API that gives access to account data, with specific methods such as batch-adding leads with contacts and companies and linking incoming leads. Webhooks can be subscribed to via API, and there are separate VoIP and chat-source APIs. Nothing in the evidence claims or shows that the API matches what the UI can do, and parts of the platform (SalesBot visual editor, widgets) are UI- or SDK-centric. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement or coverage map, evidence of API coverage for automations, scheduling and analytics, a machine-readable OpenAPI spec (the probes found none), and independent hands-on corroboration of breadth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: CRM API is a set of programming tools that allows developers to access client's data and other important information within the CRM and use it to create unique solutions.
The method allows you to add leads with contacts and a company to your account in batches.
This method allows linking an incoming lead to an existing lead.
Webhooks allow users to subscribe to certain events (such as a contact change or a new task) in Kommo, either manually or via API.
